Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and my esteemed colleagues of the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary: I am Dave Haggan and I have the honor of representing the people
of Senate District 10, which includes three municipalities in Hancock County and nine
M municipalities in Penobscot County. On behalf of the Judiciary, I am pleased to sponsor LD
1997, An Act to Authorize Issuance of Securities to odernize and Consolidate Certain
Court Facilities.
Those of us on this committee know all too well that many of our courthouses are in serious disrepair. To ensure safe, efficient, and equitable access to justice, we must prioritize the
repair and modernization of these facilities.
I agreed to sponsor this bill on behalf of the Judiciary because conditions at some courthouses have reached a critical point. Last year, the Newport District Court was forced to close due to unsafe mold conditions, requiring parties to travel to Bangor instead. The
closure of local courthouses create a real barrier to justice for the people they serve.
I urge you to support LD 1997. A representative from the Judiciary will follow and answer
any questions you may have. Thank you for your time today.

Judicial Branch testimony in favor of

199-7, An Act to Authorize Issuance

of Securities to Modernize and Consolidate Certain Court Facilities:

Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Judiciary, my name is Julie Finn and I represent the Judicial Branch. I would like to provide some brief testimony in support of Judicial Branch bill LD 1997.
Some of you will remember that last session this Committee passed out LD 924, a bill
that amended 4 MRSA � 1610-I. This was the Maine Governmental Facilities Authority
("MGFA") bond authorized by the Legislature several years ago to allow us to build new court facilities in Belfast, South Paris and Biddeford. LD 924 allowed us to take any extra funds from
that bond to use toward other courthouse projects, especially in Newport. Unfortunately, there
ended up being no extra bond funds available under that bond, so LD 924 did not help us to fund
any additional projects.
With the assistance of Senator Haggan, the Judicial Branch has introduced this bill, LD
1997, which amends 4 MRSA � 1610-Q. This is the statutory section that authorized MGFA to
issue a bond for new courthouse facilities in Ellsworth, Skowhegan and Lewiston. To the extent that there are excess funds available from this bond, we are asking that the language of the statutory section be modified so that we can use these excess funds for additional courthouse
projects, including re-establishing a court location in Newport.
The courthouses listed in the original bond will receive full and priority funding. However, allowing the Maine Judicial Branch to use any excess funding to support courthouse projects like Newport would be helpful in providing a mechanism to more efficiently and
effectively address facilities issues at our courthouses.
This bill will not have a fiscal note. There is no general fund money involved. The debt
service is already funded in the budget; it will not increase.
Thank you for your time. I would be happy to answer any questions.

Testimony in support of LD 1997, An Act to Authorize Issuance of Securities to
Modernize and Consolidate Certain Court Facilities."

Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn and distinguished members of the Judiciary
Committee. I am Representative Kenneth Fredette and I represent the towns of Dixmont, Etna, Plymouth, Corinna and my hometown of Newport.
I come to you today in support of LD 1997, "An Act to Authorize Issuance of
Securities to Modernize and Consolidate Certain Court Facilities."
This legislation represents a responsible and forward-looking investment in
Maine's judicial infrastructure and in the communities that rely on it.
The allocation of funding for a new courthouse in Newport is particularly
important. A modern, consolidated courthouse will improve efficiency, safety, and
accessibility, while ensuring that justice is administered in a setting that reflects the professionalism and dignity of our court system.
By authorizing the issuance of securities now, LD 1997 allows us to address
critical infrastructure needs in a fiscally prudent manner rather than deferring
necessary investments.
For these reasons, I strongly urge the committee to support LD 1997 and advance
it for passage.
Thank you and I'll be happy to answer any questions you may have.

District 33 Dixmont, Etna, Newport, Plymouth and Corinna
